Floating-point equality is an unsuitable universal oracle: PyTorch documents differences between mathematically equivalent batched and individual computations. [Numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/numerical_accuracy.html). Recommended protocol: calibrate numerical thresholds on separate, trusted clean users; freeze thresholds before assessing the 32 users/category. Compare aligned scores using a declared absolute-plus-relative tolerance, |a−b| ≤ atol + rtol·|b|; choose tolerances for the output scale rather than accepting defaults. [NumPy isclose](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.isclose.html). Calibrate the maximum discrepancy across each user’s prespecified mutation suite to address multiple comparisons. Keep structural assertions exact—dataset routing, candidate identities, padding/readout indices, checkpoint compatibility—and report their failures separately; never enlarge numerical tolerances to absorb them. These are proposed design choices, not guarantees established by the documentation.

Repeated mutations within a user are clustered observations, not additional independent users. Report category-specific false-alarm and detection rates with explicit denominators; for nondegenerate outcomes, resample whole users within categories when bootstrapping the macro-average. [Cluster-robust inference](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jeconom.2022.04.001). At zero alarms or perfect detection, ordinary bootstrap intervals collapse. For a prespecified binary user-level endpoint and 32 independently sampled users, exact binomial calculations give a one-sided 95% false-alarm upper bound of 1−0.05^(1/32)=8.94%, or detection lower bound of 91.06%; two-sided 95% intervals are [0,10.89%] and [89.11%,100%]. [Clopper–Pearson method](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy-1.15.0/reference/generated/scipy.stats._result_classes.BinomTestResult.proportion_ci.html). These bounds concern the defined user-level endpoint, not independent mutation-level performance; perfect observed detection does not establish universal defect detection.
